#4195. Top War tier list - Every hero ranked

Updated on November 18th, 2026 - Version: 1.685.0

In Top War, there are quite a lot of things that you could consider 'farmable', and in certain situations, heroes might be considered one of these things. And since there are just so many heroes out there, it could be quite difficult to choose a handful and make them your number one priority.

Don't despair though, below we've compiled a Top War tier list of all the best heroes in the game so you can choose the best ones according to your needs. The heroes can provide specific buffs and their kit can be extremely good in certain situations, but if you really want some additional info about these heroes, I've got you covered.

Most of the heroes on the Top War tier list are SSR Before we take a look at the Top War tier list though, I'll start by mentioning that the rarity of the heroes (SSR, SR, and R) plays a very important role in the game. The higher a hero's rarity, the more troops can join them in battle (SSR heroes can take a lot more troops than R heroes).

Therefore, it shouldn't come as a surprise that all the top-tier heroes are SSR. If you want to get SSR heroes too, all you need to do is keep playing the game - even as a f2p player you are bound to get a few eventually!

All the heroes have a type - some of them are Air Force heroes, some are Army heroes, and others are Navy Heroes. In the tier list, you will find them all divided by their type, so it will be a lot easier for you to pick the best ones based on what they should specialize in.

If you want to learn more about the game, make sure you check out our other Top War articles!

Maximo - A powerful hero that will greatly enhance any air force units and can quite literally change the entire course of a battle. He's a premium hero who is worth investing in, and by all means, one who can work on the offensive and defensive front.

Selina - She's a good hero thanks to the amazing buffs she provides, and if you manage to max her out, she greatly increases the maximum HP of other units, as well as their attack. Serval - Another broken premium hero that can make life a living hell for enemies. She's especially good when paired up with some of the other top-tier heroes, since they can stack their stats.

Preycis - This Army hero is great for aiming at the back-row enemies and is one of the best at specialising in that. He doesn't have a whole lot of other buffs (when compared to other heroes), but the sheer amount of damage dealt to the back row cannot go unnoticed. Shinji Ikari - A highly versatile hero, he can be obtained for a limited time only, but during that time, it's crucial to get him. He can be used for pretty much any type of content and has an ability that grants indestructibility for two rounds, which is definitely worth it. Optimus Prime - Another collab character that is impossible to overlook is Optimus Prime, the best Transformer out there (correct?). He can also grant an indestructibility buff, and when maxed out, is absolutely top-tier.

#4194. Black Mesa’s Latest Update is the Next Best Thing to Half-Life 3

Another year is coming to an end, and (as you and I have gotten used to by now) there’s still no Half-Life 3 in sight. You’d think that 22 years after the release of Half-Life 2, it would hurt any less, but nope.

In a bid to soothe aching hearts and Gordon Freeman enthusiasts all around the world, the wizards over at Crowbar Collective have put out a new update to Black Mesa, making the 2020 love letter to Half-Life look better than ever.

This update, branded a ‘red letter day’ by the developers, focuses first and foremost on visual improvements. Crowbar Collective has managed to make the game look better, while also significantly improving its performance in the process.

After around 20 years at Treyarch, Call of Duty Zombies writer Craig Houston has been laid off, prompting tributes from fans and former colleagues.

In a showcase by the developers, scenes previously clocking around 130 FPS now reach 170 FPS. It’s not clear how these improvements will scale on different hardware, but expect to see noticeable changes across the board.

On the eyecandy side of things, interiors have now been updated to use parallax-corrected cubemaps (PCC). This technique turns static reflections into dynamic ones by adjusting them based on the player’s perspective. As a result, it adds a lot of depth to interiors while not incurring costs on the performance side. Translucent materials like glass have also been updated to have light behave realistically as it passes through.

Another year is coming to an end, and (as you and I have gotten used to by now) there’s still no Half-Life 3 in sight.

While interiors got plenty of jazz, there have also been major improvements to the game’s environmental lighting as a whole. Crowbar Collective has improved the Source Engine’s light bouncing, making indirect illumination behave more realistically. Outdoor scenes have received image-based lighting, using HDR to bring more accurate outputs.

As a love letter to Valve’s magnum opus, it’s only natural for Black Mesa to cater to the company’s handheld console. Following the update’s performance improvements, Black Mesa has received the Steam Deck Verified badge.

The latest update to Black Mesa has modernized the user interface to make it behave better with stick controls, benefiting both Steam Deck and PC users who play with controllers. According to Crowbar Collective, keyboard and mouse have also been refined. Nostalgics can still pick the classic Half-Life menu from the Steam Workshop.

The popular Blue Shift mod by HECU Collective, which tells the game’s story through the eyes of Barney Calhoun, has been updated to be compatible with the latest version of Black Mesa.

For now, this massive update to Black Mesa is all we have until the yearly ritual of hoping for a Half-Life 3 reveal at The Game Awards. Earlier this year, Valve composer Mike Morasky alluded to a certain game codenamed ‘HLX’, which some of the more hopeful types have taken to be a working title for the much anticipated sequel.

That is not the first time Morasky has run his mouth about the HLX project, so maybe, just maybe, this time it’s for real. Until more evidence surfaces, you’ll find me playing Black Mesa.

Black Mesa is available via Windows and Linux platforms via Steam.

#4193. Dota 2 returns to Esports World Cup 2027 as PARIVISION chase a first repeat title

Dota 2 will return to the Riyadh-hosted Esports World Cup in 2027, though dates, format and prize money are still to come. The title has never been won twice, and its prize pool has fallen at every edition so far.

Dota 2’s place at Esports World Cup 2027 was announced without dates, a prize pool, a format or any invited teams. The whole event is listed for July to August 2027.

The 2026 tournament had originally been planned for Riyadh before it was moved to Paris on 20 May 2026.

The first edition, Riyadh Masters 2024, carried a US$5,000,000 prize pool. In 2025 Team Spirit took US$1,000,000 from a US$3,000,000 pool in a 16-team event. The 2026 tournament ran from 7 to 19 July with 24 teams. That field was eight teams larger than a year earlier.

The winner still takes a large share. PARIVISION collected US$750,000, or 37.5% of the pool, plus 1,000 Club Championship points. Runners-up BetBoom Team received US$340,000 and 750 points, Liquipedia reported.

Those points feed into a larger prize. In 2026 the Club Championship paid US$30 million across the top 24 clubs. The champion club received US$7 million from an overall event prize pool of US$75 million. AG.AL won it with 5,300 points, stopping Team Falcons from winning a third title in a row. For organisations weighing the cost of a Dota 2 roster, that club prize is part of the calculation.

Not every club is staying. Falcons released all five players from the roster that won The International 2025, according to Timesaver.gg.

No club or player has won the event’s Dota 2 title more than once. Each of the three editions went to a different club with a different roster. Gaimin Gladiators beat Team Liquid in the 2024 final. A year later, Team Spirit swept Team Falcons 3-0. As the 2026 champions, PARIVISION now get the first chance to defend the title.

PVISION are your Dota 2 at EWC26 Champions! 👏 pic.twitter.com/34U67Oaj7G

— Esports World Cup (@EWC_EN) July 20, 2026

Their rivals arrive in form. Team Spirit went out of the 2026 event before the final. A month later, they won The International 2026 in Shanghai. Yatoro and Collapse became the first players to win three Internationals. Team Yandex finished third at both the 2026 Esports World Cup and The International. After signing ATF, they won PGL Wallachia Season 9 and BLAST SLAM VIII.

The route into the event is taking shape. The organiser’s Road to EWC qualifier programme for 2027 aims to involve 1.8 million players across more than 400 events. Qualifier slots for each game will be announced later. Counter-Strike 2, already confirmed for both 2027 and 2028, will hold a 32-team event in Riyadh from 20 July to 1 August 2027.

#4192. The fastest cars in CSR Racing 2, in every tier

Updated with the very best cars to race in 2026

Updated on November 18th, 2026 - Version: 6.7.2

Want to quickly compare stats on all the cars in CSR Racing 2? Then this is the guide for you.

Below, we've listed all the base stats for every car and highlighted which wins in each category. R stands for Rep Bonus, and F is for Fusion Slots.

Obviously, every car can be completely changed through upgrades and tuning, but these starting numbers give you a good indication of that car's overall abilities. It provides a quick glimpse at the stats, which might just be enough to help you pick out which car to choose to purchase next.

We've also included some thoughts on which are the best cars in CSR Racing 2 - both rare imports and those you can buy with in-game cash.

Just click through below to find out the fastest cars in every tier.

Many great choices in this category. At first glance, it seems like the Golf GTI MK1 is a clear winner, especially as it also has a 6% RP bonus and eight fusion slots. However, it must be won in the Rare Imports lot, which means it's a lot harder to come by.

On top of that, the fastest car so far is the Ford Mustang Boss 302 with e.c level 50, which means, even though it's not as fast early on, it can make it up in the later stages.

The Veloster Turbo R Spec is also a decent choice, but can only be purchased with (150) Gold.

The M235i Coupe is a fantastic car for Tier 2, especially since you can buy it for just $75,000. It's light and has high power, but you'll need to upgrade your tyres to bring the grip up.

Potentially, the Mercedes-Benz 300 SL Coupe can be the fastest in this tier and by quite a big margin. Not early on, though. The same goes for the Ferrari 250 GTO and Aston Martin DB5.

If you want Tier 2's best vehicle, you'll need to earn the F-150 from the Rare Imports lot.

The Ferrari California 30 is obviously still one of the best Tier 3 cars in class - no wonder it's being kept back as a prize.

So if you can't win that, the SRT Hellcat at 825 G is a good choice with its high power, low shift time, and strong grip. If you only have dollars to spend, get the RS 5 Coupe.

At level 50, the Pontiac GTO "The Judge" is the fastest car in this category. The BMW M2 (G87) Coupe "M Performance" is right behind it in second place. As you would expect, any variant of the Civic Type R is going to be fast! This is one of my favourite categories, as there are several good choices.

The GT-R (R35) Premium looks like a pretty good vehicle for this tier. Not only is it affordable, but it has an amazing grip (too much, perhaps?!) and a low shift time. You'll need to work on power and lowering the weight with a lighter body.

The Viper ACR is another good option: it has great power for the tier, a low shift time, and 23 Fusion Slots.

Right now, the Rocket Bunny is looking more attractive than ever, but the big Grand Cherokee Trackhawk is tempting too.

At this point, the game has some amazing cars to use, and the latest releases push performance to the limits. These are by far the fastest cars in CSR Racing 2. The Bugatti Chiron is a fantastic choice, as is the FXX K, but launch cars such as the Bugatti Veyron and One:1 are still great.

If you don't want to rely on Rare Import lot wins, the Aventador LP 700-4 is a good bet with its high power, strong grip, and its relatively lightweight to boot.

Regardless, though, there's no doubt you'll have fun with vehicles like the 'Cuda "TorC" in CSR2.

#4191. Legendary game creator Vince Zampella has passed away

Vince Zampella, co-creator of Call of Duty, and a veteran studio head responsible for some of the biggest franchises in the world, is gone.

Vince Zampella, known for co-creating the Call of Duty series, among many other roles, has died. Zampella, 55, died in a car crash in Los Angeles on Sunday. The fatal crash killed him, along with the occupant of his car.

According to NBC, Zampella’s Ferrari hit a concrete barrier after leaving a tunnel in the San Gabriel Mountains, north of Los Angeles. Zampella was unfortunately trapped in an ensuing car fire, and the passenger was ejected.

Vince Zampella is one of the industry’s most prolific creators. His storied career is long, and is responsible for some of the biggest shooter franchises in history. It started with Medal of Honor in the 90s, a game that changed WW2 shooters forever.

Zampella later co-founded the legendary Infinity Ward in 2002, the team that would go on to redefine multiplayer shooters forever. Infinity Ward is the studio responsible for the Call of Duty series, which remains one of the biggest games for publisher Activision, and the entire industry.

Zampella then left the studio he founded in 2010 following a major fallout with Activision. He, along with longtime collaborator, Jason West, went to rival publisher EA to form Respawn Entertainment.

Respawn went on to create the Titanfall series, and later Apex Legends. The studio is responsible for non-shooters, of course, like the third-person action game series Star Wars Jedi. Zampella was instrumental in making the game possible, having hired God of War 3 director Stig Asmussen to helm a team within Respawn out of a desire to diversify the studio’s output and prove he can do more than make shooters.

Zampella had only recently met with journalists and peers at The Game Awards, where Battlefield 6 was nominated for multiple awards. Battlefield 6 is the most successful game in series history, in part as a result of Zampella’s leadership. The legendary leader was given the reigns of the struggling multiplayer shooter franchise in 2021, with a goal of finding a viable future.

Zampella’s sudden death has shaken the industry, and many mourn his loss as the news started spreading.

“We are heartbroken by the loss of Vince Zampella, a creative leader whose work shaped generations of players and helped define what modern shooters and action games could be,” EA said in a statement.

“While his impact reached far beyond any one game or studio, we will remember Vince for how he showed up every day, trusting his teams, encouraging bold ideas, and believing in Battlefield and the people building it. We are deeply grateful for his leadership, his generosity, and the care he brought to everything he touched, and we will carry that forward with us.”

#4190. The Video Games And More You Should Play This Weekend – October 30, 2026

Welcome to Devil's Night, the night before Halloween, where video games are best served scary. After tomorrow night – Halloween proper – no more scary video games allowed. At least not until mid-September, 2027. I'm sorry, I don't make the rules. Below you will find our weekend gaming recommendations (which is actually surprisingly light on scary games – apologies), but before that, here are some of the biggest stories of the week.

Phantom Blade Zero is one of the best action games I’ve ever played, and it’s certainly one of the most impressive to watch. Beijing-based developer S-Game uses China’s Wuxia brand of action (which was actually banned for some time during the 20th Century by the country’s government) to create a stylish, fluid, and hyper-engaging combat system. It will constantly leave you in awe that action combat can look this good. But looks aren’t everything. Fortunately, Phantom Blade Zero delivers on all fronts, with weapon mechanics so detailed that picking up a new blade can feel like unlocking a new character in a fighting game. The story won’t blow your socks off, but it’s certainly engaging and enticing enough to bring you through Phantom Blade Zero’s 40 or so hours of content. If you’re not interested in the “perfect ending,” which is the only satisfactory one in my opinion, you can complete the game in less than 30 hours. S-Game mixes high-octane combat with sprawling and rewarding exploration to create a must-play during this already busy season of games. You can read more of my thoughts in the Game Informer Phantom Blade Zero review, and if you are hopping in this weekend, be sure to check out my list of Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks I wish I knew before starting it.

If you have any fond memories of IllFonic’s ill-fated Friday the 13th: The Game as I do, you simply must play the studio’s latest, Halloween: The Game. It is essentially Friday the 13th with Michael Myers instead of Jason, but with a decade of lessons learned from the team’s teeth carving in other horror properties and games. You’re either Michael or a citizen; the former wants to kill you and all the NPCs in various suburban maps, while the latter must rescue as many NPCs as possible while staying alive themselves. It’s that classic cat-and-mouse formula IllFonic is the master of, but with all the style, substance, and synths of John Carpenter’s Halloween masterpiece. Plus, Halloween: The Game features IllFonic’s first crack at a single-player campaign, and while it’s largely a tutorial for playing as Michael, if you’re a Halloween mega-fan like me, it’s worth checking out if only to take part in some of the film’s most iconic kills. You can read more of my thoughts in the Game Informer Halloween: The Game review here, and if you’re hopping in this weekend, there’s a new map, additional Halloween-themed cosmetics to unlock, and more waiting for you.

Overwatch is in the midst of its Halloween event, which have always historically been pretty interesting. This year it's Mystery Madness: Graveyard Games. In it, you begin by picking one of three characters in a random role. And then, as the game progresses, you choose perks that upgrade, alter, or completely change what your character can do. It can get really chaotic where by round three characters like Orisa might be three times her normal size or Torbjorn might have placed a giant turret on Mercy's making her a flying death machine. There are also Halloween skins, as well.

Tom the Postgirl is an odd little adventure that I'd recommend to fans of Untitled Goose Game. You play as Tom, a creepy girl who's tasked with delivering packages to the people of her wacky town, which is depicted with storybook-style illustrations and a color palette limited to black, white, and red. On the surface, you're delivering packages, but the game's real story is based on Tom's tendency to peep where she shouldn't, peering into townsfolks' windows to watch their odd lives. On house is full of kids who live like dogs; another has a couple with a bizarre obsession with tickling. You never know what each window might reveal, and I quickly sympathized with (and enabled) Tom's compulsion. You also have the capacity to cause quite a bit of trouble by stomping on flowers, haphazardly snipping strings and cords, or even stealing packages and using them for your own mischievous purposes. It's a pretty short experience, completable in just a few hours, making it a nice palate cleanser between the massive releases at the end of the year.

This Devolver Digital-published game has a simple but head-turning premise. You’re a profoundly angry woman who returns to her small hometown armed with nothing but a sledgehammer, which she uses to smash everything in sight. The town is also inhabited by robots possessing human consciousnesses. Swinging the hammer can either punch holes through walls or, with enough force, reduce entire buildings to rubble. But why is she doing this? Why is she so mad? A big part of Virtue and a Sledgehammer’s allure is its fascinating and well-written tale about the protagonist’s strained relationships with her sister and mother. Learning more about their lives requires you to keep smashing, but the more you learn, the more you begin to question whether smashing everything is actually a good idea.

This bizarre indie blends fun match-3 puzzle-solving with tower defense gameplay wrapped around a funny but surreal story. The match-3 gameplay involves sliding tiles to match geographic elements like castles, trees, and rivers to collect resources that feed into the tower defense portion. Depending on how the board looks when the puzzle portion ends, you send troops (sustained by the resources you collected) to attack/defend against rival castles and gather more items; board positioning determines how well this can go. The two mechanics feed into each other to create a fun loop that grows in complexity as new mechanics are introduced. Did I mention the game is also very weird? The silly tale centers on a medieval court designating you the chosen savior to rescue their lost queen (and many other tasks), and the dumb tone adds personality to a sometimes dry genre. Titanium Court charmed and impressed us when it launched on PC earlier this year, and now console and mobile players get their chance to hold court.

Sword of the Sea is a beautiful, 2025 game about surfing through the sand atop a floating sword. It recalls Journey, the emotional 2012 PlayStation game, which makes sense as it comes from the artists and developers that worked on that game, developer Giant Squid. Giant Squid also made 2016's Abzû and 2020's The Pathless. It's a talented team and Sword of the Sea maintains that reputation. And now you can play it on Switch 2. You can read my full review of the game (though this review pertains to the PlayStation 5 version) right here.

Cities: Skylines arrived on PC more than a decade ago, but is still revered as one of the greatest modern city-builders. Even now, three years after the sequel's release, Paradox continues supporting and porting the original game. A couple years after its initial release, Cities: Skylines received a strong console port, which did an admirable job of adapting the controls to gamepads, but the Switch version was always the weakest of the bunch. As of this week, Switch 2 owners can play a less compromised version, expanding the Switch's 9-tile limit to a much larger 25-tile limit, as well as better performance and textures, better control panels, and a ton of DLC and added content. And on top of that, if you own the Switch 1 version, you get a deep discount on the Switch 2 version.

While not specifically about this new Switch 2 version, you can read our original reviews of the base PC version here, and the base console version here.

Minecraft has held its dominant spot in pop culture for so long that it's easy to forget a simple fact about it: the game is awesome. This week, it's coming to Switch 2, giving potential miners another platform to explore procedurally-generated caves in. You've certainly heard of it, and you've probably played it, but I still feel it often doesn't get the flowers it deserves in high-level critical discussions about games, despite its regular cadence of major updates. The opening gameplay loop is so satisfying that for many of my peers, whether they regularly play video games or not, it's only a matter of time before they boot up a new world again. While you can never play the game for the first time again, if you haven't checked it out in a couple years, you might be surprised by the amount of new blocks, materials, and mobs they've added in recent updates. And if you've never played before, the Switch 2 launch is as good a time as any to see what all the fuss is about.

The card game incarnation of Arkham Horror remains one of the best narrative-driven and horror-themed tabletop games around, and it's an easy recommendation if you're looking for something engaging to dive into on Halloween night. Rooted in the monsters and mysteries of the Cthulhu Mythos, this living card game is built on major core sets and expansions. But unlike a TCG, each new installment has the same cards included, fueling the cooperative adventures you'll undertake together with your fellow players. Last year Arkham Horror: The Card Game did something of a soft relaunch for a chapter 2 of its narrative, and that new core set is an ideal place to jump on  play. Players each control an individual investigator as they explore arcane and weird mysteries, confront monsters, and unfold plots of cultists, ancient entities, and forbidden lore. For fans of cosmic horror storytelling, it's an easy pick.

#4189. MSI 2027 heads to Valencia as Riot reshapes Split 1 with First Stand: All In in China

Riot will take the Mid-Season Invitational to Spain in 2027, bringing a top-tier League of Legends event back to Europe for the first time since the Worlds 2024 final in London. Its one-off, expanded First Stand in China will also change Split 1 for the LEC, with the full details due in January.

Europe will host a top-tier League of Legends event again in 2027. Riot set out its international calendar on 13 November, the eve of the Worlds 2026 final. The Mid-Season Invitational goes to Valencia. London’s staging of the Worlds 2024 final was the last time the continent held an international League of Legends tournament.

For British fans, that puts a top-tier event within Europe next year. Riot has not yet given dates or ticket details for the Feria de Valencia event.

Spain’s last international League of Legends event came in 2019. That year, Madrid’s Palacio Vistalegre staged the Worlds quarter-finals and semi-finals. Valencia has never hosted one before.

China will stage First Stand: All In at the start of the 2027 season. Riot calls this single edition its largest tournament ever.

First Stand 2027 had originally been given to Southeast Asia. The bigger format took it to China instead. Southeast Asia will now host the event in 2028.

The change reaches every regional league, including the LEC. The larger event will change Split 1, just as Fnatic, G2 and the other LEC teams rebuild their rosters. In 2026, First Stand ran from 16 to 22 March, between the two regional splits. A bigger event at the start of the year leaves less certainty about how that window will look in 2027.

Riot has not yet said how many teams will take part or how they will qualify. Until then, LEC teams are building squads without knowing how many European places are on offer.

Worlds 2027 will be shared between two countries. The Swiss Stage goes to Nagoya, Japan. The quarter-finals and semi-finals move to the Suwon Convention Center in South Korea. The title decider goes to Seoul Arena, which is still under construction.

The arena was 81% built on 23 October. Work is due to finish in May 2027, with the venue opening in June 2027.

The city is backing the event with public money. Seoul has set aside 1.369 billion won (about US$1.02 million) in its proposed 2027 budget to host the Worlds final and Fan Fest, Sheep Esports reported.

#4188. Grand Theft Auto 6 Review: a Once in a Generation Open-World Achievement

Grand Theft Auto 6 delivers an enormous open world, a gripping story, a vibrant Vice City and an astonishing range of activities.

If there’s one thing Rockstar can never be accused of, it’s rushing out Grand Theft Auto VI. It’s been so long since the (still incredible) GTA V launched that there are people who weren’t born at the time who are now teenagers (no, you’re not old enough to play yet, son, and go to bed!).

It’s not like Rockstar wasn’t busy during that time — they’ve been constantly updating the ever-growing Grand Theft Auto Online and also happened to release one of the greatest westerns of all time in Red Dead Redemption II. Yet all of the many years of development somehow becomes immediately apparent the second you pass the title screen. Put simply, this is one of the largest and most ambitious games ever created.

GTA 6 centers around the complicated personal and professional relationship of two criminals, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, and their journey through the realistically hard-to-succeed-in world of Vice City. That’s about the only story element I’m comfortable sharing, however, as this is a game that begs not to be spoiled and to be experienced as fresh as possible.

GTA VI’s main story is full of crazy twists and turns, surprising emotional beats, and yes, absolutely hilarious moments that push boundaries and envelopes. Along the way, you’ll meet a cast of colorful characters that will quickly endear themselves to you and ones you’d commit many virtual felonies to defeat out of seething hatred.

While the campaign is gripping and exciting all the way through, there are so many stories just waiting to be discovered in GTA VI. It feels like a living, breathing world which is all the more impressive considering there are basically no loading times or slow down upon entering a loaded save.

There’s a ton of traffic through the roads (so much so that you can’t just easily blaze through like a bowling ball as easily as in previous games), the drivers get actively mad if you crash into them, and there are NPCs going about their days on every corner. You could make a whole game into simply approaching NPCs and seeing what they’re up to — there are some surprisingly interesting happenings going on and it’s rare that even the most minor of characters repeats themselves.

From DMA Design to GTA III, GTA V, and RDR2, let's take a look back at how Rockstar Games changed open-world gaming and why GTA 6 has so much to live up to.

While you can follow the main story all the way through, complete tons of side quests or simply take part in what the most depraved of us do and make the game into a rampage simulator, there are so many activities here that almost any one of them could be focused on as a full game. There’s diving for treasure, bird watching, fishing, customizing cars and oh so many other things that are fully fleshed out and not just throwaway afterthoughts.

In fact, just existing in the game is so complex now that GTA has basically become a life sim. Upon awakening, you can eat, make coffee, watch TV, play video games, workout, watch a show, do home repairs, feed pets and enough other tasks to make a list of them as long as a full review.

It’s incredibly cool for the world to feel so realistic that you literally sometimes get stressed out from knowing you have to do a chore and can’t just go run people down (I guess I am one of the depraved ones after all). Sometimes an hour is spent in GTA VI literally lifting weights, drinking a protein drink, grocery shopping and laying down in bed doomscrolling. While that might not exactly be the sentence to sell you on the game, the fact that GTA VI is just that deep and manages to make it all enjoyable to carry out truly speaks to the attention to detail at play.

The realism also carries over into the gameplay mechanics themselves. Driving feels more realistic than it ever has. It’s easy to get wanted stars and hard to shake the cops, and people will get actively pissed off at you for doing the wrong thing. In fact, it’s realistic to the point that some might not have as much fun as they did in previous titles as you will think twice before hijacking a random car or even parking it in the wrong place (yes, the fuzz can be called on you for leaving your car at an NPC’s house).

Just existing in the game is so complex now that GTA has basically become a life sim.

It goes beyond simply just blazing through the world doing horrible things and hoping a cop doesn’t see it — there are immediate and severe consequences to your actions now.

That being said, it’s hard to criticize Rockstar for the game being too realistic, and once you adapt to its ebb and flow, this new realistic GTA experience feels all the more enveloping as it stimulates the anxiety, stress and fear synapses as much as the happiness ones, making successful accomplishments in the game all the more rewarding.

It’s impossible to review GTA VI without touching on the music, and if I had my way, this entire review would just be speaking about that. But as I don’t want to risk you clicking out since we could really use those GTA page views, I’ll keep it short.

The score itself is composed by famed French electronic duo, Justice, and is like an aural hug to the ears. The instrumentals during key action scenes are some of the best heard since HEALTH’s stunning Max Payne 3 score and get the adrenaline pumping.

The included original songs Justice recorded are so expertly crafted to sound like ‘80s hits that I was literally googling the lyrics thinking I had found long lost ‘80s songs before realizing it was actually Justice. Considering I’m big Justice fan who’ve seen their live show multiple times, that says a lot that they even fooled me.

Rockstar has released GTA 6’s launch trailer, spotlighting Jason and Lucia while confirming Justice as the composers of its original score.

It’d be fair to judge a GTA by its radio stations as they play such an integral part in the experience and are heard for literally hundreds of hours by most players, so thankfully there’s another incredible lineup here. There’s a channel for everybody — ranging from buttrock to country to reggae to classical music to many, many more.

Fans of past channels like Radio Broker and Radio Mirror Park will be happy to hear that there’s another hipster/indie style channel in GTA VI dubbed “Stockyard FM” which plays music from the likes of Hot Chip, Nation of Language, !!! and even debuts a new song from the aforementioned HEALTH. Flash FM quickly becomes a favorite as well, focusing on high energy dance pop and electro pop from artists like Billie Eilish, The Ting Tings and more.

Finally, Circoloco Records is a commendable addition featuring smooth throwback-style electronic music from Rockstar’s own record label. But expect to hear a fantastically curated soundtrack no matter which station you jam out to, with artists ranging anywhere from The Weeknd to Steve Winwood.

With how many flawlessly-executed mechanics and elements to GTA 6 there is, it’s hard to find faults. There’s not even many glitches that occur, which is shocking for an open world game of the magnitude.

Possibly the only criticism would be that it's so complex and ambitious that the learning curve is steep, and even after dozens of hours in the game, it’s easy to forget how a certain mechanic works or which button does what at times. Of course, criticizing something for being so deep proves difficult and at the very least perhaps a good problem to have in the end.

Rockstar has minimized the complexity as much as they could by providing an easy-to-access control list at all times and basically devoting the first twenty or so hours of the story as a backdoor tutorial.

Considering how enormous the scope of GTA 6 is, it’d be easy to forgive it for having visuals not up to snuff, yet it boasts some of the most realistic character models seen in gaming and uses them throughout all of the beautifully-choreographed in-game cutscenes.

The way the characters are rendered give them a certain unique realistic element that has never quite been captured before — from unique body types to random skin marks to life behind the eyes. As good as the characters look, the environments might look even better with everything from trees to the pavement itself rich in detail. There’s also incredible lighting work at play that makes everything pop like you’d expect Florida, er, Vice City to.

While it may seem impossible for anything in our universe to live up to the hype and anticipation Grand Theft Auto 6 has garnered, Rockstar has done the impossible. GTA VI offers more in a single package than any video game before it, blowing past its status as one of the best action games of all time into one of the best life-sims of all time. And one of the best driving games of all time. And one of the best…birding…games of all time? It may sound like hyperbole, but GTA VI is so chock full of content that it feels like several fully-fleshed out games in one. And that’s not to mention it actually does have several fully-fleshed out games within a game inside of it. GTA VI may not completely reinvent the wheel, but it fully commands it, delivering an enormous adventure that’s chock-full of enough things to keep you busy until Grand Theft Auto VII (please, Rockstar?). The last thirteen years were more than worth the wait and make Grand Theft Auto VI go down as an unparalleled achievement in video games.

#4187. Love and Deepspace 5.0 update brings together all five love interests for the first time

Love and Deepspace is getting a big update to celebrate its second anniversary, and there's a lot to dig through.

If you can believe it, Love and Deepspace is almost two-years-old, and Infold Games is celebrating the moment in a few major ways. The Throne of Eros update brings the game up to version 5.0, and it’s one for fans of all love interests.

For one, this is the first time all five of them are brought together. The update is also adding some important new features, alongside anniversary events, and more.

Throne of Eros also doubles as the new Wish Pool, which is the one that has all of the game’s love interests in a single banner. This is a limited-time affair, of course, but it’s not the only thing you should look forward to here.

There’s also the Memory Growth Bonus, another limited-time event that you can take advantage of to grow your Memories. The even bigger news is that you can target your Wishes through the Xspace Echo, which lets you select five Memories to create your own pool from. You can use this to get any Memories you might not have, of course.

On the topic of Memories, you’ll also be able to unlock new second anniversary KV Memories, as part of a Yearly Highlights Event that will let you look back on your own journey with the game over the past year.

On the story and narrative side, Throne of Eros adds two new main stories, with new branches for Xavier, and Rafayel. There’s even a narrative-specific event that will run throughout the anniversary period, through which you can earn two daily outfits for each of the five love interests.

The celebrations also extend to new anniversary content like mail, and video calls. You can purchase a Yearly Pass, and check out some new arrivals at the Lunar Shop.

Beyond the anniversary content, version 5.0 also adds a new feature to the game: Home, which essentially offers a hub to get you directly to interacting with love interests that doesn’t have to do with combat or story.

You can also expect various other quality of life updates that touch on the Journal, Phone Moments Search, Resources Quick Cleanup, and new Tete-a-Tete that should make interacting with all of them more streamlined.

While this is a special banner, you should brush up on how banners work in Love and Deepspace if you’re unfamiliar. As always, it’s never not a good idea to check our Love and Deepspace codes page for some freebies.

#4186. Thrifty Business review - "The coziest management sim you'll ever play"

I never thought I'd come across something that manages to impress me to this extent - until Thrifty Business, at least. And let me tell you: I was beyond impressed. So, this is not just a simple Thrifty Business review; this is me telling you why you need to give it a try.

I play a lot of games. And by a lot, I mean A LOT. So, at this point, it takes quite a bit for something to genuinely surprise me.

I expected a cute little shop management sim (as per the Play Store images). Maybe something to play for a few hours and decorate a few shelves. Well, it didn't happen quite like that. I ended up spending far more time than I'd expected rearranging furniture and getting excited over witchy items.

In essence, you can buy unwanted items from NPCs in the form of mystery boxes. Then, you place them on the shelves and organise them by category. Later on, you can even organise events and expand. That's it.

Honestly, what's not to love? Grab your tea and blanket and get cosy - we'll talk gameplay! In terms of gameplay, you have all the freedom you need as a shopkeeper. You can genuinely make the place feel like your own. From finding the perfect spot for an item to rearranging displays, you're the boss.

You can even redecorate as much as you like - there's no restriction on that (thankfully), so in a way, you can play this in your own way. I mean, you can even skip decorating altogether and just play for the dialogue or for making money.

Personally, I'm always going to choose decorating over anything else, even at the cost of buying additional items.

On the topic of additional items, Thrifty Business doesn't try to turn running a shop into a stressful experience. There's no pressure to maximise every penny or deal with impatient customers.

Even if you end up making no sales in a day, the system still has a way to keep you progressing by offering a free mystery box every day. Not that they're particularly expensive (at the beginning, at least), but it's little details like this that make me appreciate the thought put into the experience.

Just a fair warning though: it's the kind of sim where you tell yourself "I'll play for another ten minutes", only to realise an entire hour flew by. The pixel graphics: love at first sight Can we please talk about the aesthetics?

The colourful 90s atmosphere makes the entire experience feel like a warm hug.

As someone who grew up during that time, seeing all those nostalgic items brought into 2026 put a smile on my face. I'd almost forgotten all about the Slinky!

Since I mentioned it, let me make one thing clear: there are a lot of items you can acquire in Thrifty Business. I mean A LOT. With so many of them, it's hard not to appreciate the sheer amount of work that must have gone into designing all those individual sprites. Not everyone's cup of tea - but maybe everyone's cup of hot cocoa? I have to admit, Thrifty Business understands exactly what kind of experience it wants to offer. It's not one of those fast-paced tycoons where you rush to make millions from the get-go.

That might not make it into everyone's favourite list, but it is bound to make it into some. If you're over here reading this and you have someone special in your life who likes Stardew Valley, then Thrifty Business is something you can definitely surprise them with.

Really, sometimes, all you need is to escape into a cute little world, put things on shelves, decorate to your heart's content, and call it a day. Life is too fast-paced sometimes anyway, and Thrifty Business can be the escape that is one tap away. You need to play with the sound on The audio deserves some love too, and I believe Spellgarden Games did an amazing job creating a soundtrack that perfectly complements the sim. I honestly couldn't fault it at all, and I'm usually the type to turn the sound off after spending more than five hours with a game. Not this time, though...

An ode to the queer community As if the cosy atmosphere wasn't enough, I absolutely adore the queer representation woven into this.

From the story (which you should absolutely read - I won't give you any spoilers) to the item categories and even character creation, there's something about the sense of community you get in this little virtual world that gives you a fuzzy feeling inside. Not too many games celebrate individuality, self-expression, and simply being yourself in a way that feels "just right".

Now, if you'll excuse me, I have a shop to rearrange. Again.

#4184. Genshin Impact Version Luna 4 introduces three new playable characters, including the long-awaited Moon Maiden Columbina

The first major Genshin Impact update in 2026 is almost here, bringing characters we've been waiting a while to play, and more besides.

Genshin Impact’s latest Special Program has spilled all the beans on the game’s next major update, Luna 4. The update, which arrives on January 14, kicks off 2026 with several bits of new content, including some previously-teased characters.

Dubbed Traveler on a Winter's Night, Luna 4 introduces three new playable characters, and brings back The Lantern Rite event to celebrate the beginning of the new year.

The first new arrival in Version Luna 4 is Columbina Hyposelenia, the Moon Maiden. Columbina is a 5-Star Hydro Catalyst wielder. Her kit revolves around supporting the squad via Lunar Reactions. She can trigger coordinated Lunar Reaction DMG, even when she’s off the field.

The Moon Maiden’s special ability, Lunar Domain, further boosts all Lunar Reactions by applying a DMG bonus, including summoning more thundercloud strikes for Lunar-Charged reactions. Columbina is also capable of converting Electro-Charged, Bloom, and Hydro Crystallize reactions into Lunar Reactions, as well as revive fallen squad members.

Speaking of elemental reactions, new in this version is Lunar-Crystallize, a new reaction that’s triggered when Geo meets Hydro (under certain conditions). When triggered, Lunar-Crystallize summons three Moondrifts near enemies. When triggered three times, Moondrift Harmony gets activated, dealing Geo DMG to enemies caught in its radius.

Then there’s Zibai, an Adeptus from Liyue. Zibai is another 5-Star character, a Geo Sword wielder. Zibai can, through entering a special state where they can build up energy, unleash an Elemental Skill that deals Lunar-Crystallize DMG.

The longer the fight goes on, the more Lunar-Crystallize reactions are triggered, the higher (and more often) the damage of Zibai’s Elemental Skill becomes.

Luna 4 continues the Nod-Krai story arc, with a big confrontation with Il Dottore. This is the focus of the new Archon Quest, completing which will earn you a new outfit. There’s a gameplay element to that new chapter, too, with the reveal of Piramida, a new area north of the region. Piramida is the headquarters of the Lightkeepers.

The first phase of Luna 4’s Event Wishes will, unsurprisingly, feature Columbina. It’ll also include reruns of Ineffa. The second phase is when Zibai becomes available, alongside another newcomer: Illuga, a 4-Star, polearm-wielding Geo Lightkeeper. The second phase’s rerun will be Neuvillette, who’s also going to have a new outfit in the shop at a discount.

Version Luna 4 brings back the annual Lantern Rite event, taking place in the mainland of Liyue. The event features its own set of minigames with unique rewards, alongside new stories of the Adepti.

All around Liyue Harbor, you’ll be able to place Xiao Lanterns and inscribe them with messages for others to read. You’ll also earn some Fortune Coins from Auspicious Treasure Trees, which you can later exchange for gifts.

All players will receive 1,600 Primogems through the in-game mail. If you log in regularly, you can earn up to ten Intertwined Fates. Lantern Rite has a new outfit for Yaoyao, which is also where you have a chance to earn one 4-Star Liyue character for free.

Finally, you can look forward to the new Classic Mode in Miliastra Wonderland, which lets you invite select Teyvat characters to join you.

#4183. Vampire Survivors tier list - Ranking characters from base game and DLCs

Each DLC brought different characters and we have decided to rank each one and rank them on the Vampire Survivors tier list according to their late-game power.

Updated on November 18th, 2026 - Version: 1.16.111

Since the release of Vampire Survivors, people have been widely discussing things like "Who are the best characters in the game?" and other burning questions. There are, god knows, how many characters at the moment, but even then, this list can still expand with every update. Picking the most powerful character is essential to enjoying Vampire Survivors, and we are here to help with that.

Potent characters will mean an easier time, so if you're not looking for a challenge, they're the way to go. If you're playing with any of them, you can kill enemies much more effectively and win even if you are a beginner. Below are the best characters in Vampire Survivors. Also, feel free to check our Dead Cells weapons tier list as well as this tier list for Capybara Go.

About Queen Sigma Even though Queen Sigma can't pick up Golden Eggs like other heroes, she is still one of the most powerful characters, and it wouldn't be wrong to call her the best character without a doubt.

She uses the Victory Sword, which is one of the game’s most potent weapons. After levelling up, she gets +1% Might and +1% Growth, allowing her to become much more powerful. The main feature of Queen Sigma is her 333 max health, allowing her to survive longer.

About Red Death Red Death is the fastest and scariest hero in Vampire Survivors. The high speed makes this character suitable for finding Relic locations and fighting hidden bosses. Red Death uses the Death Spiral that can be easily combined with Axe in the same run. Its main feature is the 20% Might increase and the 100% Movement increase. These stats make Red Death one of the most potent heroes in Vampire Survivors.

Pungola is a mighty Vampire Survivors character that has two primary weapons: Phiera Der Tuphello and Eight The Sparrow. The hero gets +1% Might every level and can be unlocked by opening a special coffin in Mad Forest. Also, you should cast the spell “flymetothemoon” in Forbidden Scrolls of Morbane to unlock this hero.

Ambrojoe is an easily attainable hero that uses La Robba as a primary weapon. This character has average stats and no special abilities, making him the best option for beginners. We have to note that the weapon looks an awful lot like a Kinder Egg - we're actually not sure if it's an easter egg or not.

Dommario can be a good option for beginners due to his powerful defence and attack stats, but the main disadvantage of Dommario is speed. It is one of the slowest characters you can choose.

Megalo Menya Moonspell is overall the best character in Legacy of Moonspell DLC due to her combination of survivability and damage.

What stands out particularly is her invincibility, meaning she cannot take damage at all during certain periods. That said, this comes with a limitation; she will disappear when the current time limit expires. This makes her particularly powerful for clearing stages quickly.

Je-Ne-Viv is considered the most powerful character in Tides of the Foscari DLC, and that's why she's at the top of this part of our Vampire Survivors tier list. She has a unique weapon called Insatiable, which scales with Magnet and Greed stats, and comes with the Shadow Servant. Her abilities deal significant area-of-effect damage, making her a powerful character overall.

Crewmate Dino gains permanent stat boosts whenever any player's weapon reaches its max level. This ability makes him especially powerful in co-op mode, making him the best character in the Emergency Meeting DLC.

Megalo Impostor Rina has high base stats, special weapon mechanics, and the ability to scale through all phases of the game. Her toolkit is ideal for those who enjoy a playstyle that rewards aggressive tactics and strategic planning.

About Colonel Bahamut Colonel Bahamut stands out because of his great passive bonuses, like +100 Max Health and +50% Might. His weapon, Metal Claw, allows for significant area damage, making him the best character in Operation Guns DLC, capable of scaling effectively with Greed and Curse mechanics.

About Alucard Alucard is S-Tier and one of the best characters in the Ode to Castlevania DLC due to his high damage output, versatility, and healing abilities. His weapon mechanics allow for powerful area control, making him a top-tier choice for most runs.

Sonia Belmont is the other top-tier character in Ode to Castlevania. She has excellent scaling potential and powerful weapon synergies. Her ability to deal consistent dps while maintaining survivability is what makes her so good.

About Vlad Tepes Dracula Vlad Tepes Dracula has a deserving top position on this Vampire Survivors tier list since he is a character with high damage output and abilities that enhance survivability. His skills allow him to deal significant area damage, making him a standout choice for many players.

About Lisa Tepes Lisa Tepes provides excellent support with healing abilities and buffs that can sustain her and allies throughout runs. Her versatility and ability to boost stats make her invaluable in longer gameplay sessions. About Cornell Cornell has strong offensive capabilities with transformation mechanics that allow him to adapt to different combat scenarios effectively. His versatility makes him a solid choice for various builds.

About Cosmo Even though Cosmo looks cute, he is one of the deadliest heroes in Vampire Survivors. The main feature of this character is that he does not have a primary weapon. So, you have more customisation options using Cosmo compared to other heroes. About Leda The primary weapon for Leda is the Holy Land, the improved version of the Magic Wand. She can equip both weapons to reach the highest effectiveness in the same run. Leda also has Passive Bonuses, which you can find below:

Gyorunton is another dragon in Tier S. It uses the Bracelet to kill enemies and has a special ability - Gyorunton can evolve weapons much faster than other heroes using Treasure Chest. Also, this hero has 300 Max Health, which is exceptionally high compared to the classic 100 Health Points.

About Smith IV Smith IV is a scary character who uses Vandalier as a primary weapon. This hero has +100% Luck and gets +1% Luck at every level, which is a unique ability. And for such a decisive boost, Smith IV pays with his stats.

About Gain Boros Gains Boros is a mighty dragon that uses Heaven Sword as the primary weapon. This character gains +2% Growth every time you level it up, making Heaven Sword more powerful.

And that’s our complete Vampire Survivors tier list. As you can see, the game has a significant diversity of exciting characters, and 3 of the best heroes in Vampire Survivors are Queen Sigma, Red Death, and Big Trouser. Bilibili Gaming beat Gen.G in Brooklyn to win the 2026 League of Legends World Championship, the LPL's first world title since 2021. Added to their First Stand trophy, the result gives a Chinese side a double that no team had managed since 2016, just as Riot takes the 2027 season opener to China.

Bilibili Gaming are world champions. The LPL side needed four games to beat Gen.G in New York and win the club’s first Worlds title. The result ends a run of four straight LCK world titles. It also gives the LPL its first world crown since EDward Gaming won in 2021.

BLG took the hardest possible route. They knocked out all four LCK teams at the event: Hanwha Life Esports, Dplus KIA, T1 and Gen.G. Every Korean side that travelled to the tournament went home after facing them.

The final turned early. BLG levelled the series at 1-1 by winning a 53-minute second game. It was the longest game of the whole tournament. Gen.G had reached the final with two 3-0 knockout wins, over LYON on 4 November and Invictus Gaming on 7 November.

For Knight, the MVP award closes a loop. The BLG mid laner lost the 2024 final to T1. Two years later, he finished on the winning side.

The runners-up looked inward after the defeat. At Gen.G’s post-final press conference, Chovy said the team had broken its own rules. Duro, playing his first Worlds, regretted that they had dropped their drafting plan.

Gen.G still leave with US$800,000 as runners-up. Semi-finalists T1 and Invictus Gaming received US$400,000 each. Riot ran the event from 15 October to 14 November with 19 teams.

Gen.G’s admission points to the draft as a weak spot. The figures support a narrower reading too. Gen.G swept both knockout opponents before the final. Against BLG, they could not hold the lead after taking the opening game.

Worlds was BLG’s second international trophy of the year. In March they won the First Stand Tournament in São Paulo. They beat G2 Esports 3-1 in that final and collected the US$250,000 top prize.

Winning both events makes BLG the first team since SK Telecom T1 in 2016 to take more than one major international title in a year.

Our first Summoner’s Cup. It’s finally coming home.

The calendar also tilts towards China. First Stand will open the 2027 season as First Stand: All In, a one-off expanded event. Riot calls it the largest tournament it has ever produced. The event was first announced for Southeast Asia. That region will now host First Stand in 2028 instead.

The 2027 Mid-Season Invitational will be held in Valencia.

#4181. Shigeru Miyamoto Proclaims November 1 is Pikmin Day, Pikmin 4 Demo Coming To Switch 2 Soon

This morning, Nintendo shared some updates related to the Pikmin franchise and has officially claimed November 1 as Pikmin Day, starting today and moving forward presumably forever.

Aside from the announcement of Pikmin Day as a general idea, Pikmin creator Shigeru Miyamoto appeared on camera to remind everyone that Pikmin 4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy is coming November 12. A free demo for the game, which will include one standard level and two Dandori Academy levels, will be available on November 2.

The Switch 2 version of the game (you can read Game Informer’s Pikmin 4 review here) will have improved visuals and take advantage of the Switch 2’s mic to let you say things like “Rush” and “Go to work” to Oatchi. The Dandori Academy side of the game is essentially time trials you can practice, and then on Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays, you will have one chance to post your best time. You can read more about the Switch 2 version of the game here.

Miyamoto also shared that the mobile game, Pikmin Bloom, is also getting a fairly substantial update soon with secret caves. In Bloom, players will be able to find maps that reveal caves that you can send your Pikmin into to battle and find treasure. You can also find maps for Bloom by playing Pikmin 4. Caves will be coming to Pikmin Bloom later this year.

The Pikmin Day presentation also reminded viewers that every Pikmin game is available on Switch and Switch 2, though no announcements or hints were made implying that Pikmin 1 and 2 would be coming to the Nintendo Switch Online subscription service, which includes GameCube games on Switch 2. Those games can be purchased individually on the eShop.

Finally, Miyamoto brought actress Fuka Koshiba on the presentation (best known for voicing Kiki in Kiki’s Delivery Service) to share her appreciation for the Pikmin franchise (she likes to knit Pikmin hats that she shares on social media) and introduce a Pikmin short film. In the short, a Pikmin interacts with a toad, but I won’t spoil what happens. Miyamoto promised more shorts are on the way and in the future, they will be found in the Nintendo Today app.

Unfortunately, the stream concluded without a single reference to 2017's Hey! Pikmin. I wouldn't expect it to get a port to Switch 2 anytime soon.

#4180. GTA 6 Ties for the Best Reviewed Game of All Time

Scott Baird is a Contributor from the UK with over a decade of video game writing experience.

Rockstar has finally proven the doubters wrong, as Grand Theft Auto VI is officially tied for the best-reviewed video game of all time, with only Nintendo’s greatest retro title managing to keep up.

Expectations for Grand Theft Auto VI were sky-high going in, especially after being delayed on multiple occasions, with Take-Two and Rockstar promising that the game needed more polish and would be worth it in the end. There were some doubters, but the fact that Take-Two was leaving money on the table meant that most fans had faith it would live up to expectations.

The embargo for Grand Theft Auto VI went up as soon as the game went live on New Zealand’s Microsoft Store, and the scores are in. It seems that Rockstar is ending 2026 with a bang, as Grand Theft Auto VI has obliterated the competition, at least in terms of reviewer opinion.

Denkiworks explains why Tanuki: Pon's Summer launched between Zelda and GTA 6, and why the small studio believes the risk was worth taking.

The Metacritic page for Grand Theft Auto VI is live, and the results are in. Grand Theft Auto VI’s MetaScore is 99, making it tied for the best-reviewed game of all time, with a huge range of 10/10s from outlets worldwide.

One outlet that gave Grand Theft Auto VI a 10/10 is DualShockers, with Steve Hennley writing, “While it may seem impossible for anything in our universe to live up to the hype and anticipation Grand Theft Auto 6 has garnered, Rockstar has done the impossible. GTA VI offers more in a single package than any video game before it, blowing past its status as one of the best action games of all time into one of the best life-sims of all time.”

Grand Theft Auto VI’s MetaScore is 99, making it tied for the best-reviewed game of all time, with a huge range of 10/10s from outlets worldwide.

The only game to match Grand Theft Auto VI’s MetaScore is the original version of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the Nintendo 64, which also has a 99. Funnily enough, the game’s remake came out this year, and it scores slightly lower than Grand Theft Auto VI, capping out at a 96 on Metacritic.

That being said, a trip to Hyrule might be the only option for a lot of people, as Grand Theft Auto VI is currently a PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S exclusive. This means that Nintendo Switch 2 and PC owners will have to find out games to play. Maybe it’s time to break out Garfield Kart and pretend he’s running over civilians?

It was always likely that Grand Theft Auto VI would score well, considering Rockstar’s amazing library of titles and the sheer amount of time and money that went into its latest game. The delays might have been frustrating, but if the result was the best-reviewed game of all time, then it was worth it.

With the help of XBOX Cloud Gaming, even last generation's XBOX console will be getting in on the fun.

The question now is what the fans will think, as only people in New Zealand can currently play the game. Oh, and the people on Xbox Series X/S who have suddenly traveled to Middle-earth and switched their region to New Zealand (don’t worry, no one will tell John Microsoft). After all, it’s not unheard of for the critical and audience reviews to differ greatly.

The verdict from the fans will filter in over the next few days and weeks, but until then, Rockstar and Take-Two can lean back and know they have a stacked accolades trailer ahead of them, and that Vice City will have millions of visitors over the upcoming holiday season. If the reviewers are correct, a once-in-a-generation game has arrived, and it’s time to dive in.

Grand Theft Auto 6 delivers an enormous open world, a gripping story, a vibrant Vice City and an astonishing range of activities.

#4179. Heartopia captures the hearts of Animal Crossing and The Sims fans to become the No.1 free download across 50 countries

Heartopia is officially the first big mobile launch of 2026, as the game grabs the attention of millions worldwide.

Heartopia, the new cosy life sim from XD Games, has officially arrived on mobile, right on schedule. If you’ve been keeping up with Heartopia news, you’re likely already aware that the game has pushed back its Steam release to an indeterminate point in 2026.

Doesn’t look like it mattered much, however, as this has already been a big launch on iOS and Android — it probably helps that PC players aren't being entirely left out of the fun, since the game is already available there via XD's own cross-device platform TapTap.

XD Games announced today that Heartopia has reached the top spot on the App Store’s downloads page for free games, and it managed to do so in more than 50 countries and regions worldwide.

The developer is celebratig by offering players a lot of free stuff. If you're feeling lucky, you’ll find new outfits and furniture in three gacha banners (Gilded Acorn Exhibitions): Polar Hymn, The Frostguard, and Coolplayism.

XD Games says you can expect regular updates to add more content, through Fashionwaves and Festivals. In fact, the first season - Winter Frost - is already penciled in for sometime in late January, and it’s going to add appropriately wintery activities like ice skating and snowman-building.

In February, a My Little Pony collaboration event will kick off, bringing new inspired outfits, and vehicles to the game.

Heartopia is a clever mix of Animal Crossing, and The Sims. It’s a free-to-play life sim where you can create your own character, dress them up, build a home for them (and decorate it), and go about town visiting and playing with other players’ characters.

The game’s main feature is the ability to take on a hobby, and seven of those are available at launch. You can dig deep into each hobby, either alone or with others, and there’s a progression track dedicated to each one.

Whether you’re among the millions who downloaded the game already, or you intend to so soon, we’ve got a set of helpful guides to get you started. You should check out how to unlock and upgrade hobbies in Heartopia first, before you get deep into finding all cooking recipes. #4178. Path to Nowhere tier list - All characters ranked

Updated on November 2nd, 2026 - Version: 1.9.54

Path to Nowhere has a considerable variety of characters you can unlock. But if you are a beginner, finding out what hero to use can be problematic. Luckily, experts across the web have created a tier list for Path to Nowhere to solve this problem.

We have similar articles like this Neural Cloud tier list and Summoners War: Chronicles tier list, where we have also ranked all of the characters by their power and abilities from the best to worst. If you're playing different mobile games, try to search around - our website is brimming with tier lists and various guides for the most popular games. WHAT IS THE PATH TO NOWHERE TIER LIST?

This Path to Nowhere tier list is similar to the ones we have for other video games. There are four tiers: S, A, B, and C. Continue reading, and you will learn more about every tier.

Most players consider Demon to be the most overpowered hero in the game. His special attack stacks a shield for him and his allies. The more health points Demon has, the more powerful protection he will create.

He also has potent attack stats, allowing him to kill enemies fast.

Nox is the most accessible hero in Tier S. She can be unlocked by completing the 14-day event. Nox has incredibly high DPS and a passive ability that decreases your enemies’ defence. Moreover, Nox increases attack points upon killing enemies, which is one of the best abilities in Path to Nowhere. So, make sure to obtain this hero as soon as you can.

Labyrinth is the only hero in Tier S that has a B rarity. So, you can unlock her even if you don't play the game daily. Labyrinth is a damage dealer who takes the primary role in a team. She can break enemies’ shields and even destroy Demon’s shield.

Even though Baiyi has less DPS than Nox, she still can deal a lot of damage in a short period. Moreover, her skill significantly increases critical rate boost. She is also one of the fastest heroes in Path to Nowhere.

Langley is a top-level hero because of her particular skill. It provides you with an AoE attack that can hit a 3x3 area. So, Langley is a perfect option if you want to fight against bosses or groups of enemies.

Eirene is a magical attacker that probably has one of the best passive abilities in the game. While using an auto-attack, she creates a black hole that hits a 3x3 area. The only disadvantage is that Eirene is weak in melee fights.

Hamel is the only healer in Path to Nowhere that is worth being in Tier S. She has an AoE healing effect that helps keep your team's HP topped up in battle.

Countless Chelsea is one of the most complex heroes in Path to Nowhere. But in good hands, she brings excellent results. Countless Chelsea can summon a panther that can be used as a shield. Also, she has damage reduction, allowing her to take a lot of punishment and still survive.

The main feature of Demolia is her health points. She can quickly increase them and, after that, heal herself, which significantly increases her survivability. The only reason why she's not in Tier S is that there is a limit on her HP boost and healing.

Even though Serpent looks cute, she is one of the deadliest heroes in Path to Nowhere. While using a standard attack, she applies a slowdown effect to enemies and increases her speed. Moreover, when there are no enemies near Serpent, she will raise her attack.

RouLecca has poor DPS and can only deal damage using critical attacks, but she can increase her crit rate and damage while attacking.

Zoya is the Tier A hero most likely to appear in Tier S in the future. She has a 3x3 AoE attack that can deal significant damage. Zoya also has a lot of health points and has no problem killing enemies in short range. But the best thing about Zoya is her passive skill. It increases her attacking speed, making her suitable even in the later stages of the game.

Pricilla can summon a clone who helps her during battle. Additionally, she has high DPS, allowing you to kill enemies quickly. Unfortunately, her lack of health points doesn't make her worthy of becoming Tier S.

Hecate's ability has long range and hits every target in this range, which is extremely powerful. But Hecate doesn't have good survivability, so you should be careful while using her.

Aerial is the only healer in Tier A. The only difference between her and Hamel is that she is universal. Aerial has increased damage, which enables her to fight against enemies. And for increased damage, she gives up her healing capabilities. So, Aerial can't heal as effectively as Hamel.

Victoria is a hero with really significant damage. However, she forgoes health points for such a high attack capability. She will lower her health points to gain more attacks and kill enemies more effectively.

Luvia Ray is the most classic damage dealer in Path to Nowhere. She has high stats and a passive skill oriented toward increasing attack. Overall, she is a mighty hero who will always bring benefit to your team.

Crache has one of the best special attacks in the game. The AoE can deal a high amount of damage quickly. Moreover, this attack has an unblocking effect, so that opponents can't dodge it. The only disadvantage of Crache is that she has purely physical stats. Therefore, she must be complemented by powerful characters who can deal a lot of damage.

The best thing about EMP is that this hero is free. You can obtain her by completing the first chapter of the story. As for battle, she is perfectly suitable for the role of a background hero. Her special attack can wipe out low HP heroes and provide additional buffs for your team.

Tier B includes the following characters:

You can find out more about the most powerful heroes from Tier B below.

Cinnabar is a unique combination of powerful abilities in one character. She can create a 3x3 range shield protecting allies. Even though this shield doesn't have many health points, using it can still be handy during battles. Overall, Cinnabar is pretty powerful. She has a strong multiplier, allowing her to win battles easily.

Ninety-Nine is one of the best tanks in Path to Nowhere. You can exchange her health points in order to deal damage to enemies. On top of that, her extraordinary ability will reduce her health to get a significant attack bonus.

Sumire hits four times in a row in the same direction with her Special Ability. This special is extremely powerful on small maps, making Sumire more effective there. Also, she increases her damage when someone is opposite to her. Moreover, there are no limitations on increasing damage.

Even though Wolverine can't play the central role in the team, his slowing-down effect allows him to be effective even with higher-tier characters. Wolverine has special traps that stun enemies. These traps have a high range, making this hero super helpful.

Tier C includes characters that aren't recommended to use, even if you are a beginner.

The main feature of Pepper is her powerful attack speed. She can even increase it using a particular skill. But the main problem with Pepper is that she has no other stats to boast about.

There is nothing special about Gekkabijin. She has no powerful stats like the Tier S characters. Her unique ability provides her with additional attack and shield, but it isn't good enough to be competitive nowadays.

Even though the game has different characters with distinct abilities, it's best to only use the ones at the top of our Path to Nowhere tier list if you can - Tier S and Tier A - since they consistently perform the best.

Thank you for reading this guide - hope you find it helpful! And while you are here, make sure to read our Path to Nowhere beginner's guide as well.

#4177. Diablo 4's long-awaited Tower and its Leaderboards enter beta today, and there's no PTR funny business this time

Diablo 4's first big moment of 2026 is nearly upon us, and it's one feature many have been looking forward to for actual years.

Diablo 4 is about to deliver on Blizzard’s years-old promise to add a challenging, leaderboard-driven experience to the action RPG. The beta for The Tower, and its associated Leaderboards are about to kick off.

As recently revealed, the new experience launches today at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 7pm GMT. This is a beta version that arrives alongside update 2.5.2.

This early launch won’t offer the full experience, and it’s mainly designed to get it into the hands of players early so that Blizzard could get as much feedback as possible and incorporate it into the final version.

The beta is available to everyone, which is a nice change from the usual rigmarole players would have to go through to get the PTR build and play on a different branch. The Tower, and Leaderboards will be available only in the Seasonal Realm, however. Indeed, the plan is to build on what’s there with each future season, so it’s best to think of it as a seasonal experience.

The Tower is about as simple of an activity as you can get in an action RPG. The goal is to climb as many floors as you can as quickly as you can, all while battling increasingly difficult mobs.

You need to reach and beat the Tower’s final boss before you can call it a run. The Leaderboard will then show your time, and let you see how well you did compared to other players.

The Tower is available to anyone who completed Rank 2 of the current Season Rank. Once done, an Obelisk will appear in Cerrigar, letting you access the challenge.

The Leaderboards themselves will operate on a two-week schedule, all of which will take place during a given season. In this case, they’re going to close the day before Season of the Divine Interversion - the game’s current season - ends.

Blizzard published an updated set of patch notes that show how much has changed since The Tower, and Leaderboards first became playable in the patch 2.5.0 PTR.

Though the two new additions have been anticipated for a while, there’s not been much exciting going on in the world of Diablo 4, apart, of course, from the surprise arrival of The Paladin class, which became available in December last year to coincide with the announcement of Lord of Hatred, the game’s next expansion.

#4175. EDward Gaming part with CHICHOO and nobody as Champions core breaks up before 2027

EDward Gaming have lost captain nobody and CHICHOO, two days after releasing Smoggy to Bilibili Gaming. The VCT China partner team must now rebuild before the China Kickoff in Hangzhou in January.

EDward Gaming have parted ways with CHICHOO and captain nobody, two pillars of the side that won VALORANT Champions 2024. Both players left the VCT China partner team on the same day. EDG announced both exits on Weibo. Their exits end a five-year spell at the organisation.

The departures follow quickly on from Smoggy’s move to Bilibili Gaming. Within a week, three players had gone from the EDG roster. No replacements have been named.

Wang ‘nobody’ Senxu joined EDG on 7 September 2021. He served as the team’s captain and in-game leader. He had started out as the side’s Initiator before taking on those leadership duties. CHICHOO, whose full name is Wan Shunzhi, played the Controller role. Alongside CHICHOO, he formed the core of the only Chinese team to win Champions. That title, sealed on 25 August 2024, made EDG the first organisation from China, and from Asia, to lift the trophy. The team’s total winnings stand at roughly $1,592,287.

The pair were still central to the side in 2026. At Masters London, CHICHOO and nobody each played 12 maps. Their average combat scores were 179 and 184 respectively. EDG finished third in London and earned $125,000. Their run ended with a 0-3 defeat to Leviatán in the lower bracket final on 20 June 2026.

Where nobody goes next is not yet confirmed. Sheep Esports reported, citing sources, that he is expected to join Trace Esports for 2027. Trace’s Kai and deLb are said to be under contract until the end of 2027. If that move happens, nobody and Smoggy would both start the new season with different organisations.

The timing is awkward for EDG. The organisation was named a VCT partner team on 21 October, on a two-year contract. That deal now begins with a heavily changed roster.

The China Kickoff is an S-Tier LAN event. It is organised by TJ Sports, Hero Esports and Riot Games. The league’s partner sides make up eight places in the field, with the remaining four split evenly between visiting teams and open qualifier entrants. EDG will need a settled line-up in place to compete there.
